page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g7se.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Enhanced family, provisioned through a KVM hypervisor. The instance is powered by a dedicated 2.9 GHz Intel Xeon 8369B processor, supplying 4 vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. Memory configuration stands at 16.0 GB total, reflecting an exact 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Storage is strictly non-local with 0 GB of bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage options. Dedicated baseline network throughput is rated at 2 Gbps, and no discrete hardware accelerators or GPUs are included.

Instruction set features for the x86_64 architecture include AVX, AVX-512F, and AVX-512 VNNI, along with cryptographic offloads such as AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. Synthetic benchmarks reflect solid single-threaded performance paired with moderate multi-core capacity constrained by the low core count. The Geekbench single-core score of 1556.0 and stress-ng single-core score of 1879.48 rank in the middle 50% tier, supported by an average single-threaded gzip compression rate of 27.8 GB/sec. Conversely, the multi-core score of 3338.0 in Geekbench and the multi-core stress-ng metric of 3870.6 place in the bottom 25% bracket.

Memory subsystem benchmarks show uncached read and write bandwidths of 30.13 GB/sec and 24.19 GB/sec respectively, alongside a PassMark memory score of 1832.6. Small model (135M) LLM text generation reaches 109.67 tokens/sec, though prompt processing is limited to 406.5 tokens/sec. Operational metrics include 3.82 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and 6.17 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

The ecs.g7se.xlarge provides balanced resource density for standard business logic and lightweight network services. Because it possesses no bundled local storage and modest parallel throughput, it is best suited for decoupled web serving, application middleware, small-to-medium cache instances, and background task processing rather than heavy database or parallel compile workloads.
